label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: One transition anyone can take: any member, in any session, can write the file.
findings.why: Transition, session and the file are all new words to someone who has only built one app, and the hold file has not been shown yet.

findings.quote: That is the whole design of the brake.
findings.why: A short declarative opening that announces its own importance, followed by short sentences.

findings.quote: The one limit is the one chapter 16 found
findings.why: A forward-looking pointer to a chapter I may not have read, with no hint of what the limit means for me.

findings.quote: That line is the whole chapter in one sentence.
findings.why: The same line was already quoted in chapter 6 and is the section's second 'whole' claim after line 19, so it tells me twice what to take away.

findings.quote: rules in plain words, a scope check that catches mistakes, a second reading in the same room
findings.why: This re-lists the three sections I have just read, so the argument is said again before it is turned on the factory.

findings.quote: six attempts, each refused or failed, one of them only probable, and nothing acted
findings.why: Review step, attempt and register are not explained, so I cannot tell what was attempted or why it matters.

findings.quote: The record does not say whether one would have; it only shows that none had to.
findings.why: This reports the record in the third person, where I want the editor saying what he makes of it now.

findings.quote: It has a session, a key and a page of rules of its own
findings.why: A key is never explained for someone without a coding background.

findings.quote: Both read the hold the same way: part one final, not locked.
findings.why: A dense run of agreements (hold, locked, tasks switched off, sessions closing partial) that I cannot follow without the earlier chapters.

findings.quote: Two readers who never compared notes reached the same sequence.
findings.why: The historian's next line says the same thing again in different words.

findings.quote: each carries dev's session line, and, as this book then found on rechecking, dev's agent line too
findings.why: Commits, subjects and trailers are used as if known, and the point of the finding is lost on me.

findings.quote: the two commits that never reached the team's branch
findings.why: This paragraph is a stack of unexplained internals (reply file, branch, commits) that would make a non-programmer stop reading.

findings.quote: You can read both. That is the point:
findings.why: 'That is the point' opening, and 'You can read both' sends me to files I am not shown.

findings.quote: shortened by this book's writer in its own words: not the agent's words
findings.why: Three layers of authorship (agent, historian, writer) in one bold sentence is hard to hold before I have read a single interview.

findings.quote: I put the record check into the gate, so a wake that skipped a step failed the build for every member.
findings.why: Gate, wake, build and record check are all jargon in one sentence; this is the first interview and it reads as written for programmers.

findings.quote: The conductor named the limit itself: a second reading, not a second identity.
findings.why: The same conductor line is quoted at chapter 6 line 75, in chapter 18 and in chapter 19, so I meet it four times.

findings.quote: That catches an agent that wanders by mistake, and on the day it caught some.
findings.why: Chapter 18 gives the same scope explanation at its line 34, nearly sentence for sentence.

what_holds: 18-how-do-we-contain-this.md: the three states of the hold, 'running, held, released', are something I can picture, and 'a second reading, not a second reader' is a line I can keep.
18-how-do-we-contain-this.md: the 'Something to try' card is a step I could take tomorrow without code: write down who may stop the team and who restarts it.
19-a-second-team-reading-cold.md: the idea of handing finished work to someone with no context is something a beginner can do, and the closing card says so simply.
06-roles-as-a-cast-you-can-read.md: each member speaking in the first person, with what went wrong left in, makes the cast easy to follow.
notes: The two chapters about the factory's own team (19 and the interviews in 06) lean on the book's internal vocabulary; the opening chapter 18 is the most welcoming. Counts: see findings.
